title: Reverse-Polish evaluator
prompt: The input is a program in reverse-Polish notation: a list of instructions pair(tag, value). Run it on a stack that starts empty, in order: tag 0 pushes value; tags 1, 2 and 3 ignore value, pop the top element b and then the next element a, and push a + b (tag 1), a - b (tag 2) or a * b (tag 3). Tags are always 0..3. If an instruction with tag 1..3 finds fewer than two elements on the stack, the program fails. Return some(v) when the program does not fail and the final stack holds exactly one element v; otherwise (a failure at any point, an empty final stack, or more than one element left) return none. The empty program returns none.
